headline: Autonomous LLM agents are automating single-cell and multi-domain biological discovery
label: Agentic Ai For Discovery
summary: LLM agents and foundation models are being benchmarked and built into autonomous workflows for single-cell, microbiome, and lipid-design discovery.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the shift from static predictive models to agentic systems that propose, execute, and evaluate analyses. PantheonOS uses an evolvable multi-agent LLM framework that auto-evolves batch-correction and RL gene-panel selection algorithms for single-cell and multi-omics data. Eubiota applies RL-tuned multi-agent AI to gut microbiome discovery, reporting 87.7% benchmark accuracy and hypotheses validated in mice and IBD metagenomes. LUMI-lab couples a transformer foundation model with active learning in a self-driving platform that screens over 1,700 lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery. A benchmark of LLM-based agents on 50 single-cell omics tasks scores code synthesis, collaboration, efficiency, and knowledge integration. What is new is the coupling of autonomous optimization or experimental loops with explicit agent evaluation. The single-cell benchmark assesses agent capability rather than reporting new biological findings.
